summary: Implemented and validated a production-oriented Docker setup for the image-processing scenario using Debian Slim + multi-stage build, non-root runtime, health checks, and build-context hygiene.
evidence: Created Python Dockerfile in api/ using chosen Decision B strategy: Debian Slim base with multi-stage builder/runtime separation.
Single-stage baseline image size was captured as myservice-single:latest 327MB.
Refactored multi-stage hardened image built as myservice:latest 287MB (smaller runtime image by excluding build-time layers/tools from final runtime stage).
Added runtime hardening in Dockerfile: non-root user (appuser/appgroup) and HEALTHCHECK targeting service liveness endpoint.

Added .dockerignore and ran failure drill: with .dockerignore disabled, Docker build context transfer increased to 72.74MB; with .dockerignore enabled, context was only ~2.97kB/18.78kB in clean builds.
Runtime verification: container launched with required env vars and showed healthy status in docker ps ('Up ... (healthy)').
Endpoint checks passed from host against mapped container port 3300: GET /live returned 200 and GET /ready returned 200.
To support readiness/liveness contract, added /live and /ready endpoints in api/app/main.py (ready performs DB check via SELECT 1).
